subject: Cross-border control matrix & EU-only processing follow-up
messages:
From: Sarah Clark <sarah.clark@meditrust.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Meditrust DPO <dpo@meditrust.com>
Date: 2027-07-19T08:12:00Z
Subject: Initial ask — EU-only processing evidence and control mapping

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we start procurement, our legal and privacy teams need a concise mapping showing how Redwood ensures EU-only processing for Meditrust workloads (account data + PHI-like metadata). Specifically we need:

- A controls matrix aligned to SCCs showing technical and contractual mitigations for cross-border access (including backups).
- Evidence that backups and snapshots are stored in-region or encrypted with customer-managed keys that do not leave the EU.
- Sample audit logs / retention policy excerpts showing deletion flows.

Can you share a draft control matrix and custody diagram by end of week? If certain items require an architectural diagram or on-prem gateway description, please flag those.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Clark
Head of Procurement, Meditrust

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Clark <sarah.clark@meditrust.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-19T12:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial ask — EU-only processing evidence and control mapping

Hi Sarah — thanks, we can do that. Attaching a first-pass control matrix and a short KMS/keyflow diagram (see attachment list).

Notes / quick calls-outs:
- Hosted: For our Redwood Hosted EU offering, primary processing and KV caches are pinned to eu-central regions. Backups are stored in-region by default; snapshots are encrypted at rest.
- KMS: We support customer-managed keys (CMKs) via partner KMS in EU regions; keys can be provisioned such that key material never leaves the customer region.
- Access controls: Administrative access to EU-only workloads is restricted and audited; we can provide an export of a couple days of anonymized audit logs.

Laura and Priyom — can you confirm the backup residency language and add any technical diagrams (especially around cross-region fallback policies) into the matrix? Also Hannah — looping you for retention/deletion wording for contractual exhibits.

Next step: I can share a Drive folder and propose a 30-minute sync if that helps.

Thanks,
Jordan
Director, Security & Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-eu-control-matrix-v1.xlsx; kms-keyflow-diagram.pdf

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-20T09:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial ask — EU-only processing evidence and control mapping

Jordan / Sarah — uploading my technical annotations to the control matrix (attached as v1.1 row comments). Key points:

- Backups: Snapshot lifecycle in our EU regions is configured with an in-region retention tier. By default, we do not tier backups outside the selected EU region. For customers requiring stronger guarantees we offer a dedicated storage account in-customer-VPC (Redwood Dedicated / Private) that prevents transfer.
- Encryption: All at-rest artifacts (models, tensors, KV caches, snapshots) are AES-256 encrypted. When CMKs are used, envelope encryption is applied with the CMK only accessible via KMS endpoints pinned to the EU region.
- Emergency access: Administrative break-glass requires explicit justification and is time-limited and logged; we'll include example log entries.

I added two new tabs to the workbook: "Technical mapping" and "Evidence artifacts (sample)". The evidence tab includes a sanitized audit-log sample (audit-log-sample.txt) and retention policy snippets.

Laura
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Sarah Clark <sarah.clark@meditrust.com>
Date: 2027-07-20T11:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial ask — KMS and key residency details

On Tue, Jul 20, 2027 at 09:08 AM laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai> wrote:
> - Encryption: All at-rest artifacts (models, tensors, KV caches, snapshots) are AES-256 encrypted. When CMKs are used, envelope encryption is applied with the CMK only accessible via KMS endpoints pinned to the EU region.

Adding some implementation specifics for your legal team: 

- We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS (eu-west-1/eu-central-1) and GCP KMS (europe-westX). Keys are never exported from the KMS; we use envelope encryption so raw key material never traverses our control plane.
- Backup replication: the default behavior is in-region only. If a customer configures geo-replication, it is an explicit opt-in and captured in the contract exhibit.
- Logs: we can produce a 72-hour window of anonymized admin-access logs and a redacted S3 access-log sample for validation.

Sarah — flag whether you need formal KMS attestation language or a clause for the contract exhibit; we can produce both a short paragraph and a longer technical appendix.

Thanks,
Priyom
Infrastructure Security Lead, Redwood

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Clark <sarah.clark@meditrust.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-21T07:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft control matrix + suggested contractual language

Hi Sarah — I pulled concise deletion and retention language for the contract exhibit. Summary below (will paste final wording into the workbook):

- Retention: Customer data (input text, derived embeddings) stored in EU region for the duration of the active subscription; logs and aggregated metrics retained for up to 90 days by default unless a longer retention is requested.
- Deletion: Customers can request bulk deletion; deletion jobs are processed within 72 hours and snapshots are marked for purge in the next snapshot lifecycle (configurable, default 30 days). We will provide deletion receipts (hash + timestamp) and can attach them to a contract exhibit.
- Schrems II / SCCs: We recommend SCCs + a contractual exhibit referencing the in-region KMS and backup-opt-in controls. For higher assurance, suggest Dedicated or Private (customer-managed infra) so the contract can enumerate physical host boundaries.

If helpful, I'm available for a 30-min call to walk legal through wording. Jordan — I updated the Drive folder and left a draft exhibit in the "contract_exhibits" tab.

Hannah
Privacy Counsel, Redwood

Shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4redwood-eu
